So I was thinking about the idea of giving advantage to the attacker on attack rolls when the target has only a small amount of HP left (e.g. 10% rounded up). The premise behind it is that the target is significantly weaker than when it was attacked at full health. My curiosity lies in its balance, though. Thoughts?
[5e] [Homebrew] Advantage On Attack Rolls When Target Has A Small Amount Of HP Left?

This seriously weakens some of the characters that rely on effects that happen at low health, namely Half-Orcs, Barbarians, and Champion Fighters.

To balance this out, I feel like characters at low health should be able to get some type of advantage for this. Maybe something like this:

Characters are considered "weakened" when at 25% or less health. This is equivalent to being poisoned, except the character chooses one of the three following powers upon reaching the threshold and keeps these temporary abilities until it is healed past 50% or until it is canceled as a free action. Once these powers are canceled, a new one can be reinitialized (assuming the character's life is below 25%) as a bonus action for one stack of exhaustion :

Driven by Bloodlust: No disadvantage on attacks, and can use a bonus action to perform an extra attack. Attacks made with bonus actions from class features have advantage during Driven by Bloodlust.

Driven by Fear: Can Disengage or Dash as a bonus action. Movement is increased by 5 during Driven by Fear. Using Disengage or Dash as a bonus action from any class feature adds +5 to your movement speed for the round.

Driven by Instinct: No advantage on being hit, and can use the Dodge action as a bonus action. Using Dodge as a bonus action from any class feature makes them proficient on all saving throws and ability checks for the round (including checks made while dying).

[EDIT]: Every minute (10 rounds) of being weakened and still under the influence of one of these effects will inflict a point of exhaustion.

As a side note, there's a good 'houserule' in the DMG that suggests having "real" damage start at half HP, with upper end of life being used to indicate stress and minor cuts and the lower half indicating real damage with blood. This system works well with that houserule, with characters starting to freak out once they are starting to get carved up.

While I haven't used something like the weakened system before (at least, not without some specific intervention on the DM's part for dramatic effect) I can imagine using both houserules together would be really cool while keeping it in a system that players won't be surprised by. Hell, if they want to abuse these rules, more power to them. Lots of people are adrenaline junkies, and the characters that rely on these effects could just be addicted to the thrill of real battle.

Honestly, permanent disadvantage on either attacking or defending is a pretty big deal, and I don't foresee many people living to abuse these rules for very long.
